folder.

both directions. Do NOT merge it wholesale — main has work this tree lacks.

docs: reconcile grant-facing narratives with code gating reality (#1251)

Align GRANTS.md, DEMO.md, PROVENANCE.md and two stale code-vs-doc facts so a reviewer routed from README finds the same project the grant docs describe.

- GRANTS.md: rewrite as an audience-neutral capabilities/maturity base with a crisp split between "What Works Today" (commit/verify/proof-bundle loop + offline verifiers) and "Implemented In-Tree, Audit-/Ceremony-Gated" (ZK, federation behind off-by-default `federation` feature, anchoring). Add press-freedom + civic framing addenda so the OTF and Watauga tracks share one honest core. Remove reviewer-perception-coaching language. Resolve the offline-verification contradiction. Drop EVM SBT from the working list (it is deferred to a later phase; DB tables not yet present).
- DEMO.md: state demo scope explicitly (commit/verify/proof-bundle only; ZK + anchoring are test-suite-covered; federation off by default).
- PROVENANCE.md: split vkey fingerprints into 3 on-disk production circuits vs 2 next-phase placeholders (unified + federation_quorum, ceremony-pending / feature-gated) so there is no apparent manifest-vs-disk mismatch.
- README.md: arti-client 0.27 -> 0.31 (matches Cargo.toml).
- watauga_county_pilot_2026.md: drop retired FastAPI/Olympus-Start-Windows.cmd references; describe the Tauri 2 + Axum + pg_embed stack and start.bat/.sh.

Author: Anthony Smith
Message:
Dataset-manifest commitments + installable client CLI/SDK (ADR-0027) (#1246)

* feat(manifest): dataset-manifest commitments + installable client CLI/SDK (ADR-0027)

Adds a customer-facing productization layer on top of the existing commitment
primitives, so a lab can put Olympus in a training-data pipeline without the
desktop app or any GUI.

- crates/olympus-manifest: dataset-manifest schema + commitment. manifest_root
  is the existing Olympus SMT global root (sound inclusion AND non-membership;
  byte-identical to node output, so the existing Rust/JS verifiers and the
  document_existence/non_existence circuits validate manifest proofs unchanged).
  Compact committed document (per-shard roots + metadata; never the record list)
  so one small commit covers millions of records. Path-compressed batch builder
  (smt_batch) makes the build scale and proofs O(256); parity-tested against the
  reference SparseMerkleTree oracle.
- Incremental versions: ManifestDiff + domain-separated diff_root + parent ref
  give a structural version link; per-record inclusion/exclusion proofs in each
  version establish v2 = v1 - removed + added (the natural redaction pairing).
- clients/cli: `olympus` binary, cargo-installable, excluded from the main
  workspace. Offline core (build/prove/verify/diff/link/hash) has zero extra
  deps; network commit/fetch behind a `server` feature (reqwest + rustls).
- Docs: ADR-0027 (design), benchmark doc with measured throughput
  (1M records sealed ~35s single-threaded, proofs ~0.02ms/~30KB), EU AI Act
  training-data compliance crosswalk, and the external audit + legal memo scope.

No protocol/leaf-layout change: olympus-crypto is untouched and no golden
vectors move. The manifest layer is additive and client-side.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01NxCyZU8HUpLpd3QkmpTXT5

* fix(manifest): use sort_by_key to satisfy clippy::unnecessary_sort_by (-D warnings)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01NxCyZU8HUpLpd3QkmpTXT5

* chore(fuzz): regenerate stale Cargo.lock, pruning removed olympus-core/pyo3

The fuzz lockfile still pinned the deleted olympus-core PyO3 extension (and
thus pyo3 0.24.2), which is not in fuzz/Cargo.toml's dependency tree. The stale
pyo3 entry tripped cargo-audit on RUSTSEC-2026-0176/0177. Regenerating the
lockfile prunes the phantom crate; the vulnerable code was never built.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01NxCyZU8HUpLpd3QkmpTXT5

* feat(python): pip-installable Olympus manifest SDK with cross-language parity

Adds clients/python (`olympus-manifest` on PyPI): the pip half of the
pip/cargo-installable client. Verifies record inclusion/exclusion proof bundles
offline, hashes shards, builds a record index, and talks to a node.

- hashing.py / smt.py / proof.py: byte-exact port of the olympus-crypto domain
  primitives (leaf/node/empty-subtree, record + shard keys) and the SMT
  existence/non-existence + bundle verification. Verify-only, like the JS
  verifier; the authoritative manifest_root is produced by the Rust builder.
- client.py / cli.py: local file hashing + scan, and an optional requests-based
  commit/fetch (http extra). `olympus-py` console entrypoint.
- Parity is pinned against vectors emitted from the Rust source of truth
  (olympus-manifest example gen_python_vectors -> tests/vectors.json); 9 tests
  cover every primitive, real inclusion/exclusion verification, and tamper/
  relabel/kind rejection. All green.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01NxCyZU8HUpLpd3QkmpTXT5

* test(manifest): rename test helper param salt->variant (CodeQL false positive)

The test-only `pseudo(seed, salt)` data generator tripped CodeQL's "hard-coded
cryptographic value / used as a salt" rule on the parameter name. It is not a
cryptographic salt — just a variant byte to derive distinct keys vs values for
the same index. Renamed to `variant` (more accurate) to clear the alerts; no
hash output changes, parity vectors unchanged.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01NxCyZU8HUpLpd3QkmpTXT5

* fix(manifest,cli,python): address PR review findings

All findings verified against current code and fixed (none were stale):

Security / correctness
- diff.rs: verify_removed/verify_added now require both proof bundles to name
  the same (shard_id, record_id, version) before combining, so a valid
  inclusion proof for record A can't be paired with an exclusion proof for B to
  fake a change. Added a regression test.
- cli/scan.rs: stop following symlinks (use symlink_metadata; skip links so a
  symlinked dir can't loop/escape root and a symlinked file isn't hashed through);
  rel_record_id fails on non-UTF-8 components instead of lossily collapsing them
  (committed record ids stay unambiguous). Added a symlink test.
- python smt.py / proof.py: verifiers never raise on malformed/untrusted input —
  defensive validation + length checks return False, and verify() returns a new
  Verdict.MALFORMED for missing/ill-typed fields or bad hex. Added parametrized
  malformed-input tests.

Robustness / UX
- cli/args.rs: treat `--key=` and `--key ""` (empty values) as absent so req()
  reports them missing instead of yielding "". Added a test.
- cli/main.rs: `require()` helper validates the full set of required flags up
  front and prints the right USAGE banner if any is missing (build/prove/verify/
  diff/link).
- cli/server.rs: bounded connect/overall timeouts on the blocking HTTP client.
- bench_manifest: reject SHARDS==0 / N==0 before use (avoids div-by-zero).

Docs
- CLI + Python READMEs: clarify `commit` uploads the full canonical manifest
  blob (multipart "file"); fetch_proof is keyed by the returned content_hash.
- eu-ai-act-mapping: drop "signed manifest_root" (verification is
  manifest_root == auditor expected_root from hashing the anchored blob); scope
  the exclusion/GDPR Art. 17 row to non-membership evidence only, with a note
  that the SMT can't attest to out-of-band deletion requests.
- e2e test: assert the RootMismatch/INVALID INCLUSION marker, not just exit code.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01NxCyZU8HUpLpd3QkmpTXT5

Author: Anthony Smith
Message:
feat(zk): migrate redaction_validity to 1024-leaf depth-10 object-level scheme (ADR-0025) (#1226)

* @
feat(redaction): PDF object-level commitment (ADR-0025)

Replace the 16-chunk raw-byte redaction commitment with one Poseidon leaf
per indirect PDF object. Redaction zero-fills selected objects in place
(length + offsets preserved) so non-redacted objects stay byte-identical
and their leaves survive a real redaction.

- new olympus_crypto::poseidon::object_leaf + POSEIDON_DOMAIN_OBJ_LEAF
- new src-tauri/src/zk/pdf_objects.rs (traditional-xref parser,
  extract_objects, apply_redaction, witness_inputs)
- circuit params 16/4 -> 1024/10 (template + public signals UNCHANGED;
  only redaction vkey needs regen, other circuits untouched)
- chunk.rs deprecated, decoupled to local CHUNK_LEAVES=16
- JS verifier + Rust-generated golden vectors (byte-for-byte parity)
- docs: ADR-0025 (supersedes ADR-0023/0024), CHANGELOG, CLAUDE.md, ceremony

NOTE: unchanged per-leaf-inclusion template at 1024/10 is ~several million
constraints; likely exceeds the shared power-20 ptau. Confirm via
circom --inspect before the v1.0 ceremony.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
@

* @
feat(redaction): flat-fold redaction_validity circuit (ADR-0025, N=1024)

Per-leaf Merkle inclusion at 1024/depth-10 is ~5.4M constraints (circom2
WASM OOMs; needs power-24 ptau). Since the parameter change already forces
a fresh redaction Phase-2 ceremony, switch the inclusion check to a single
flat fold: recompute originalRoot once from all leaves (maxLeaves-1 node
hashes, heap layout binds leaf i to index i structurally). ~1M constraints,
near the power-20 boundary.

Public-signal surface UNCHANGED ([nullifier, originalRoot, redactedCommitment,
revealedCount, issuerAx, issuerAy]); node/commitment domain hashes unchanged,
so the Rust + JS leaf/root/commitment math and golden vectors are unchanged.
Drop pathElements/pathIndices from witness circom_inputs (no longer circuit
signals); struct fields retained for verify_all_paths + the deprecated chunk
caller. Docs/ceremony/setup power updated (REQUIRED_POWER 21; confirm exact
count with native circom --inspect).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
@

* @
docs(redaction): correct witness module header for flat-fold circuit

Doc-only: public-signal vector is 6, circuit takes no per-leaf paths, struct
retains paths for verify_all_paths + the deprecated chunk caller.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
@

* @
chore(redaction): lock ptau power from measured constraint count (ADR-0025)

Measured with native circom 2.2.3: redaction_validity flat fold is
- default optimization: ~2,128,373 constraints (power-22)
- --O2: 982,946 constraints, 0 linear  → fits 2^20 (shared power-20 ptau)

setup_circuits.sh now compiles redaction_validity with --O2 (only that
circuit, so other vkeys/manifests do not move) and sets REQUIRED_POWER=20.
Docs/ceremony/CHANGELOG/CLAUDE updated with the measured numbers and the
note that the circom2 WASM build cannot write this circuit (use native).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
@

* @
fix(ceremony): raise Node heap for snarkjs Groth16 setup (ADR-0025)

redaction_validity is now ~1M constraints; snarkjs zkey setup OOMs on
Node default ~2GB heap. Export NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192
(respecting any caller-set value) in setup_circuits.sh.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
@

* test(redaction): migrate round-trip + ceremony artifacts to 1024-leaf depth-10 (ADR-0025)

Tests:
  - MAX_LEAVES=1024, DEPTH=10 in zk_prove_redaction.rs
  - Subset reveal exercises corner-case indices (0, 100, 500, 1023)
  - Full reveal path retained in tampered_redacted_commitment_fails
  - build_tree scales mechanically to depth 10

Ceremony:
  - redaction_validity vkey rotated for the 1024/10 flat-fold circuit
    introduced in earlier ADR-0025 commits on this branch. New SHA-256
    bc4658832d9303353bcf86095dd64cd496c088068caa7c75e4f623a7ad045734.
  - All 5 manifests rotate because setup_circuits.sh is non-selective:
    a single run re-randomizes every circuit's Groth16 contribution chain
    hash and coordinator signature. The OTHER 4 circuits' vkey *content*
    is unchanged (LF-normalized blob hashes match HEAD); only redaction's
    circuit source rotated.
  - PROVENANCE.md timestamp + redaction line updated.

Validation: all four prove round-trips PASS under WSL against the fresh
artifacts (zk_prove_existence, zk_prove_non_existence, zk_prove_redaction,
zk_prove_unified).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(proofs): realign circomspect baseline to ADR-0025 line shifts (#1226)

The 1024-leaf depth-10 migration shifted redaction_validity.circom, moving

* feat(babyjubjub-permissive): scaffold crate + curve ops + compression

Phase 1 of the babyjubjub-rs replacement (see PR description for the
plan). Adds `crates/babyjubjub-permissive/` (Apache-2.0) implementing
the circomlib parameterization of Baby Jubjub on top of arkworks 0.6:

* `field::Fr` — prime-order subgroup scalar field over l (252-bit prime),
  same modulus as `ark-ed-on-bn254::Fr` since both curves share this
  subgroup. Defined via `MontConfig` derive.

* `curve::BabyJubjubConfig` — `TECurveConfig` + `MontCurveConfig` impl
  with the circomlib twisted-form constants (a=168700, d=168696,
  generator B8) directly on `ark_bn254::Fr` as the base field. NOT the
  untwisted `ark-ed-on-bn254` form (a=1, d=168696/168700) — same curve
  algebraically but different point coordinates, which would break
  byte-compat with every existing trusted-issuer pubkey, ceremony
  coordinator signature, SBT signature, federation co-signature, and
  Pedersen commitment.

  Cofactor 8, COFACTOR_INV taken from ark-ed-on-bn254 since the
  subgroup order matches. Montgomery companion A=168698, B=1 derived
  via standard A=2(a+d)/(a-d), B=4/(a-d) formulas.

* `compress::{compress, decompress}` — iden3 / circomlib 32-byte format
  (LE y + high-bit sign-of-x where sign = `x > (q-1)/2`). Strict y < q
  check on decompress so two on-wire encodings cannot decode to the
  same point (`from_le_bytes_mod_order` would otherwise silently
  reduce). DecompressError enumerates the rejection reasons.

Tests (8 passing):
* curve equation holds for B8
* l·B8 = O (prime-order subgroup membership of the generator)
* 8·P lands in the prime subgroup for random P
* B8 / identity / 64 random subgroup-point compression round-trips
* y ≥ q rejection
* sign bit flips between (x,y) and (-x,y)

Phase 2 (EdDSA sign+verify + frozen parity vectors against current
babyjubjub-rs) and Phase 3 (JS parity against circomlibjs) are still
ahead. Call sites still use babyjubjub-rs; deny.toml exception still
in place. This commit only adds the new crate; nothing is swapped yet.

Phase 2 of the babyjubjub-rs replacement. Adds the EdDSA-Poseidon signer
+ verifier matching circomlib's wire format byte-for-byte, plus a frozen
set of 100 parity vectors captured from the current babyjubjub-rs crate.

Algorithm (verbatim from circomlib eddsa.circom + circomlibjs):
* `scalar_pre = BLAKE-512(sk_seed)[0..32]` with RFC-8032 pruning
  (clear low 3 bits of byte 0, clear bit 7 of byte 31, set bit 6 of
  byte 31), interpreted little-endian as a BigInt
* `scalar = scalar_pre >> 3` (lands in the prime subgroup)
* `A = scalar · B8` (public key)
* `r = BLAKE-512(BLAKE-512(sk)[32..64] || msg_32LE) mod l` (nonce)
* `R8 = r · B8`
* `hm = Poseidon([R8.x, R8.y, A.x, A.y, msg])` (5-input)
* `s = (r + hm · scalar_pre) mod l`
* Verification: `s · B8 == R8 + 8·hm·A` (the factor of 8 cancels
  the `<< 3` between scalar and scalar_pre)

Critical detail surfaced during parity-test debugging: circomlib uses
**original BLAKE-512** (SHA-3 finalist, 2008; Rust crate `blake-hash`),
NOT BLAKE2b-512 (RustCrypto `blake2` crate). The original task brief
specified `blake2`, which produces different bytes for the same input
and failed the parity test on first try. Confirmed against
circomlibjs/src/eddsa.js (`import { blake512 } from "@noble/hashes/blake1"`)
and babyjubjub-rs/src/lib.rs (`use blake_hash::Blake512`). Comment in
the import explains the trap for future readers.

* feat(babyjubjub-permissive): scaffold crate + curve ops + compression

Phase 1 of the babyjubjub-rs replacement (see PR description for the
plan). Adds `crates/babyjubjub-permissive/` (Apache-2.0) implementing
the circomlib parameterization of Baby Jubjub on top of arkworks 0.6:

* `field::Fr` — prime-order subgroup scalar field over l (252-bit prime),
  same modulus as `ark-ed-on-bn254::Fr` since both curves share this
  subgroup. Defined via `MontConfig` derive.

* `curve::BabyJubjubConfig` — `TECurveConfig` + `MontCurveConfig` impl
  with the circomlib twisted-form constants (a=168700, d=168696,
  generator B8) directly on `ark_bn254::Fr` as the base field. NOT the
  untwisted `ark-ed-on-bn254` form (a=1, d=168696/168700) — same curve
  algebraically but different point coordinates, which would break
  byte-compat with every existing trusted-issuer pubkey, ceremony
  coordinator signature, SBT signature, federation co-signature, and
  Pedersen commitment.

  Cofactor 8, COFACTOR_INV taken from ark-ed-on-bn254 since the
  subgroup order matches. Montgomery companion A=168698, B=1 derived
  via standard A=2(a+d)/(a-d), B=4/(a-d) formulas.

* `compress::{compress, decompress}` — iden3 / circomlib 32-byte format
  (LE y + high-bit sign-of-x where sign = `x > (q-1)/2`). Strict y < q
  check on decompress so two on-wire encodings cannot decode to the
  same point (`from_le_bytes_mod_order` would otherwise silently
  reduce). DecompressError enumerates the rejection reasons.

* curve equation holds for B8
* l·B8 = O (prime-order subgroup membership of the generator)
* 8·P lands in the prime subgroup for random P
* B8 / identity / 64 random subgroup-point compression round-trips
* y ≥ q rejection
* sign bit flips between (x,y) and (-x,y)

Phase 2 (EdDSA sign+verify + frozen parity vectors against current
babyjubjub-rs) and Phase 3 (JS parity against circomlibjs) are still
ahead. Call sites still use babyjubjub-rs; deny.toml exception still

  untwisted `ark-ed-on-bn254` form (a=1, d=168696/168700) — same curve

  subgroup order matches. Montgomery companion A=168698, B=1 derived
  via standard A=2(a+d)/(a-d), B=4/(a-d) formulas.

  (LE y + high-bit sign-of-x where sign = `x > (q-1)/2`). Strict y < q
  check on decompress so two on-wire encodings cannot decode to the
  same point (`from_le_bytes_mod_order` would otherwise silently
  reduce). DecompressError enumerates the rejection reasons.

* feat(babyjubjub-permissive): EdDSA-Poseidon sign/verify with 100-vector parity

Phase 2 of the babyjubjub-rs replacement. Adds the EdDSA-Poseidon signer
+ verifier matching circomlib's wire format byte-for-byte, plus a frozen
set of 100 parity vectors captured from the current babyjubjub-rs crate.

Algorithm (verbatim from circomlib eddsa.circom + circomlibjs):
* `scalar_pre = BLAKE-512(sk_seed)[0..32]` with RFC-8032 pruning
  (clear low 3 bits of byte 0, clear bit 7 of byte 31, set bit 6 of
  byte 31), interpreted little-endian as a BigInt
* `scalar = scalar_pre >> 3` (lands in the prime subgroup)
* `A = scalar · B8` (public key)
* `r = BLAKE-512(BLAKE-512(sk)[32..64] || msg_32LE) mod l` (nonce)
* `R8 = r · B8`
* `hm = Poseidon([R8.x, R8.y, A.x, A.y, msg])` (5-input)
* `s = (r + hm · scalar_pre) mod l`
* Verification: `s · B8 == R8 + 8·hm·A` (the factor of 8 cancels
  the `<< 3` between scalar and scalar_pre)

Critical detail surfaced during parity-test debugging: circomlib uses
**original BLAKE-512** (SHA-3 finalist, 2008; Rust crate `blake-hash`),
NOT BLAKE2b-512 (RustCrypto `blake2` crate). The original task brief
specified `blake2`, which produces different bytes for the same input
and failed the parity test on first try. Confirmed against
circomlibjs/src/eddsa.js (`import { blake512 } from "@noble/hashes/blake1"`)
and babyjubjub-rs/src/lib.rs (`use blake_hash::Blake512`). Comment in
the import explains the trap for future readers.

  + 5 self-consistency unit tests
* examples/gen_parity_vectors.rs: one-shot vector capture from
  babyjubjub-rs. Deterministic via seeded StdRng so reruns produce
  identical JSON. Marked for deletion in Phase 4 when babyjubjub-rs
  drops out of the workspace; vectors remain.
* tests/parity_vectors.json: 100 frozen (sk, msg, pk_x, pk_y, r8x,

Phase 1 of the babyjubjub-rs replacement (see PR description for the
plan). Adds `crates/babyjubjub-permissive/` (Apache-2.0) implementing
the circomlib parameterization of Baby Jubjub on top of arkworks 0.6:

  with the circomlib twisted-form constants (a=168700, d=168696,
  generator B8) directly on `ark_bn254::Fr` as the base field. NOT the
  untwisted `ark-ed-on-bn254` form (a=1, d=168696/168700) — same curve

  coordinator signature, SBT signature, federation co-signature, and
  Pedersen commitment.

  subgroup order matches. Montgomery companion A=168698, B=1 derived
  via standard A=2(a+d)/(a-d), B=4/(a-d) formulas.

* `compress::{compress, decompress}` — iden3 / circomlib 32-byte format
  (LE y + high-bit sign-of-x where sign = `x > (q-1)/2`). Strict y < q
  check on decompress so two on-wire encodings cannot decode to the
  same point (`from_le_bytes_mod_order` would otherwise silently
  reduce). DecompressError enumerates the rejection reasons.

* feat(babyjubjub-permissive): EdDSA-Poseidon sign/verify with 100-vector parity

Phase 2 of the babyjubjub-rs replacement. Adds the EdDSA-Poseidon signer
+ verifier matching circomlib's wire format byte-for-byte, plus a frozen
set of 100 parity vectors captured from the current babyjubjub-rs crate.

Algorithm (verbatim from circomlib eddsa.circom + circomlibjs):
* `scalar_pre = BLAKE-512(sk_seed)[0..32]` with RFC-8032 pruning
  (clear low 3 bits of byte 0, clear bit 7 of byte 31, set bit 6 of
  byte 31), interpreted little-endian as a BigInt
* `scalar = scalar_pre >> 3` (lands in the prime subgroup)
* `A = scalar · B8` (public key)
* `r = BLAKE-512(BLAKE-512(sk)[32..64] || msg_32LE) mod l` (nonce)
* `R8 = r · B8`
* `hm = Poseidon([R8.x, R8.y, A.x, A.y, msg])` (5-input)
* `s = (r + hm · scalar_pre) mod l`
* Verification: `s · B8 == R8 + 8·hm·A` (the factor of 8 cancels
  the `<< 3` between scalar and scalar_pre)

Critical detail surfaced during parity-test debugging: circomlib uses
**original BLAKE-512** (SHA-3 finalist, 2008; Rust crate `blake-hash`),
NOT BLAKE2b-512 (RustCrypto `blake2` crate). The original task brief
specified `blake2`, which produces different bytes for the same input
and failed the parity test on first try. Confirmed against
circomlibjs/src/eddsa.js (`import { blake512 } from "@noble/hashes/blake1"`)
and babyjubjub-rs/src/lib.rs (`use blake_hash::Blake512`). Comment in
the import explains the trap for future readers.

Files:
* src/eddsa.rs (~350 lines): PrivateKey / PublicKey / Signature / verify,
  + 5 self-consistency unit tests
* examples/gen_parity_vectors.rs: one-shot vector capture from
  babyjubjub-rs. Deterministic via seeded StdRng so reruns produce
  identical JSON. Marked for deletion in Phase 4 when babyjubjub-rs
  drops out of the workspace; vectors remain.
* tests/parity_vectors.json: 100 frozen (sk, msg, pk_x, pk_y, r8x,
  r8y, s) tuples
* tests/parity.rs: 3 tests — pubkey derivation parity, signature byte
  parity, verify accepts every legacy signature. All 100 vectors must
  pass each test.

Dev-deps added: babyjubjub-rs (for the generator), ff_ce, serde,
serde_json, hex. All removed in Phase 4.

17 tests passing (14 lib + 3 parity).

   versionless workspace path dependencies as wildcards on *publishable*
   crates. `allow-wildcard-paths` only exempts them for unpublishable
   (`publish = false`) crates. Mark the internal crates accordingly —
   `babyjubjub-permissive`, `olympus-crypto`, and `olympus-desktop` — matching
   the existing `light-poseidon` convention. All three are internal/never
   published, so this is correct hygiene regardless.

Phase 2 of the babyjubjub-rs replacement. Adds the EdDSA-Poseidon signer
+ verifier matching circomlib's wire format byte-for-byte, plus a frozen
set of 100 parity vectors captured from the current babyjubjub-rs crate.

Algorithm (verbatim from circomlib eddsa.circom + circomlibjs):
* `scalar_pre = BLAKE-512(sk_seed)[0..32]` with RFC-8032 pruning
  (clear low 3 bits of byte 0, clear bit 7 of byte 31, set bit 6 of
  byte 31), interpreted little-endian as a BigInt
* `scalar = scalar_pre >> 3` (lands in the prime subgroup)
* `A = scalar · B8` (public key)
* `r = BLAKE-512(BLAKE-512(sk)[32..64] || msg_32LE) mod l` (nonce)
* `R8 = r · B8`
* `hm = Poseidon([R8.x, R8.y, A.x, A.y, msg])` (5-input)
* `s = (r + hm · scalar_pre) mod l`
* Verification: `s · B8 == R8 + 8·hm·A` (the factor of 8 cancels
  the `<< 3` between scalar and scalar_pre)

Critical detail surfaced during parity-test debugging: circomlib uses
**original BLAKE-512** (SHA-3 finalist, 2008; Rust crate `blake-hash`),
NOT BLAKE2b-512 (RustCrypto `blake2` crate). The original task brief
specified `blake2`, which produces different bytes for the same input
and failed the parity test on first try. Confirmed against
circomlibjs/src/eddsa.js (`import { blake512 } from "@noble/hashes/blake1"`)
and babyjubjub-rs/src/lib.rs (`use blake_hash::Blake512`). Comment in
the import explains the trap for future readers.

* feat(babyjubjub-permissive): scaffold crate + curve ops + compression

Phase 1 of the babyjubjub-rs replacement (see PR description for the
plan). Adds `crates/babyjubjub-permissive/` (Apache-2.0) implementing
the circomlib parameterization of Baby Jubjub on top of arkworks 0.6:

* `field::Fr` — prime-order subgroup scalar field over l (252-bit prime),
  same modulus as `ark-ed-on-bn254::Fr` since both curves share this
  subgroup. Defined via `MontConfig` derive.

* `curve::BabyJubjubConfig` — `TECurveConfig` + `MontCurveConfig` impl
  with the circomlib twisted-form constants (a=168700, d=168696,
  generator B8) directly on `ark_bn254::Fr` as the base field. NOT the
  untwisted `ark-ed-on-bn254` form (a=1, d=168696/168700) — same curve
  algebraically but different point coordinates, which would break
  byte-compat with every existing trusted-issuer pubkey, ceremony
  coordinator signature, SBT signature, federation co-signature, and
  Pedersen commitment.

  Cofactor 8, COFACTOR_INV taken from ark-ed-on-bn254 since the
  subgroup order matches. Montgomery companion A=168698, B=1 derived
  via standard A=2(a+d)/(a-d), B=4/(a-d) formulas.

* `compress::{compress, decompress}` — iden3 / circomlib 32-byte format
  (LE y + high-bit sign-of-x where sign = `x > (q-1)/2`). Strict y < q
  check on decompress so two on-wire encodings cannot decode to the
  same point (`from_le_bytes_mod_order` would otherwise silently
  reduce). DecompressError enumerates the rejection reasons.

* curve equation holds for B8
* l·B8 = O (prime-order subgroup membership of the generator)
* 8·P lands in the prime subgroup for random P
* B8 / identity / 64 random subgroup-point compression round-trips
* y ≥ q rejection
* sign bit flips between (x,y) and (-x,y)

Phase 2 (EdDSA sign+verify + frozen parity vectors against current
babyjubjub-rs) and Phase 3 (JS parity against circomlibjs) are still
ahead. Call sites still use babyjubjub-rs; deny.toml exception still

* fix(ci): unbreak supply-chain — scope cargo-deny + publish=false on internal crates

The `supply-chain (sbom + audit)` check failed on PR #1103 for two reasons,
neither a real supply-chain finding:

1. `cargo deny check` (all checks) aborted loading the RustSec advisory DB —
   cargo-deny 0.16.4's bundled rustsec parser can't parse a newer advisory
   entry (RUSTSEC-2026-0035). Vulnerability scanning is already done by
   `cargo audit` in the same job, so cargo-deny doesn't need to re-parse the
   advisory DB. Scope it to the policy it owns: `check bans licenses sources`
   (workspace + verifiers/rust).

2. With advisories scoped out, the `bans` check then failed: the new
   `cargo deny` step (added in this PR) was the first to run, and it flags
   versionless workspace path dependencies as wildcards on *publishable*
   crates. `allow-wildcard-paths` only exempts them for unpublishable
   (`publish = false`) crates. Mark the internal crates accordingly —
   `babyjubjub-permissive`, `olympus-crypto`, and `olympus-desktop` — matching
   the existing `light-poseidon` convention. All three are internal/never
   published, so this is correct hygiene regardless.

Verified locally with cargo-deny 0.16.4 (same pin as CI):
`cargo deny --all-features check bans licenses sources` → bans ok, licenses
ok, sources ok (workspace + verifiers/rust).

audit rounds 1-3 + ceremony integrity runtime checks (#1076)

* audit: rounds 1-3 — H/M/L fixes + ceremony integrity doc

ZK circuit changes (require setup_circuits.sh rerun on consumers):
- H-1 unified: sectionHashes[i] === Poseidon(documentSections[i])
- M-1 non_existence: keyHash as public input, bound to Poseidon(key)
- M-2 redaction_validity: in-circuit EdDSAPoseidonVerifier on nullifier
  digest; manifest carries issuer (Ax,Ay) as public inputs

Live code changes (immediate at next binary build):
- H-2 /zk/verify: reject treeSize=0 unless root == empty_doc_existence_root
  (poseidon::empty_doc_existence_root cached at startup)
- H-4 persistent SMT: NodeBackend::acquire_write_lock (pg_advisory_lock /
  tokio Mutex) + post-lock hot-cache refresh. Concurrent-writer regression
  test in tree.rs caught a real cache-staleness bug — both halves
  load-bearing.
- H-5 /ingest/records JSON commit endpoint removed (a "verifiable ledger"
  can't accept a client-attested hash); frontend migrated to /ingest/files
  (server-hashed bytes).
- M-3 multi-issuer SBT manifest via OLYMPUS_BJJ_TRUSTED_ISSUERS_JSON, with
  per-issuer valid_from/valid_until windows.
- M-4 OLYMPUS_ENV=production refuses unverified Rekor receipts.
- M-5 CircomProvingKey newtype seals prove_circom against LibsnarkReduction
  (root cause of #1011).
- L-3 OLYMPUS_TRUST_FORWARDED_FOR opt-in for same-host reverse-proxy
  deployments.
- L-7 auth.rs parse_sig_fields routes through canonical parse_fr_decimal.
- L-19 hex_to_fr strict 64-lowercase-hex (no right-align padding).
- L-21/22 babyjubjub-rs pinned =0.0.11; rand_core multi-version explainer.

Tests + verification:
- L-16/17 Poseidon parity vectors (snarkjs reference) + constants probe
  against light-poseidon's t=3 BN254 parameters.
- L-18 artifact-independent redaction parity tests (Rust-side commitment
  + nullifier locked to hand-traced reference values; runs without
  circuit artifacts).
- All four prove/verify integration tests pass end-to-end against fresh
  ceremony artifacts (existence ~1.5s, redaction ~5.5s, non_existence
  ~13s, unified ~14s).

Provenance + ceremony:
- L-20 crates/light-poseidon/PROVENANCE.md + scripts/check_light_poseidon_upstream.sh
  pinned to upstream SHA 203de7fea8209891c478d5e44254181c1472ce02; new
  light-poseidon-provenance CI job.
- proofs/CEREMONY_INTEGRITY.md operational protocol for ZK ceremony
  artifacts (atomic bundles, signed manifests, runtime checks).

Repo hygiene:
- .gitignore: .claude/worktrees/, .claude/docfixes-*/, .claude/stage-*.sh,
  mutants.out*/ — closes the accidental-submodule-commits footgun that
  bit an earlier push.

* ceremony-integrity: implement runtime checks per CEREMONY_INTEGRITY.md

Three runtime checks the doc specifies are now live:

1. Compile-time (build.rs):
   asserts blake3(LF-normalized vkey.json) ==
   manifest.artifacts.vkey.blake3 for each circuit. Build panics on
   mismatch citing both files + both digests. cargo:rerun-if-changed=
   for vkey + manifest. LF normalization makes the digest
   platform-stable (Windows checkout converts to CRLF; CI sees LF —
   without normalization the digests would never agree).

2. Runtime (.ark.zkey load):
   load_proving_key_with_manifest re-hashes the .ark.zkey before
   deserialize. ZkeyError::ManifestMismatch surfaces tamper as a clear
   prove-time error instead of "proof fails to verify" 2h later. Cache
   key is (path, expected_blake3) with double-checked-lock so two
   concurrent first-hits don't each Box::leak a 30-200 MiB key.

3. Startup (coordinator signature):
   main.rs::verify_ceremony_manifests parses each embedded manifest,
   verifies coordinator pubkey is in state.bjj_trusted_issuers (audit
   M-3), recomputes the running chain hash from contributions[], and
   verifies the BJJ-EdDSA signature. Under OLYMPUS_ENV=production any
   non-placeholder failure is std::process::exit(2); placeholder
   manifests are ALSO fatal in prod (catches binaries with real
   .ark.zkey + placeholder manifest that would otherwise slip past).
   Dev mode surfaces tracing::error! and continues so contributors
   can iterate.

Tooling + artifacts:
- New src-tauri/src/bin/generate_manifest.rs writes a JCS-canonical
  signed manifest from on-disk ceremony output. Signing-key
  precedence: OLYMPUS_CEREMONY_COORDINATOR_KEY > OLYMPUS_BJJ_AUTHORITY_KEY >
  fixed dev fallback. LF-normalizes the vkey before hashing to match
  build.rs.
- New src-tauri/src/zk/manifest.rs: CeremonyManifest schema + parse
  / check_artifact / verify_coordinator_signature helpers. Strict
  32-byte hex decode for contribution_hash via decode_hash32 (no
  silent zero-pad/truncate). 9 unit tests cover untrusted-issuer /
  tampered-chain / tampered-sig / blake3-mismatch / placeholder
  detection.
- proofs/setup_circuits.sh appends generate_manifest as step 3b
  after export_ark_zkey so re-runs produce all artifacts atomically.
- proofs/keys/manifests/<circuit>_manifest.json committed for the
  four ceremony-bound circuits. federation_quorum is placeholder
  until its ceremony runs.

CodeRabbit review pass on PR #1076:
- CEREMONY_INTEGRITY.md: clarified manifest.sig is BJJ-EdDSA over
  BLAKE3(canonicalize(manifest.json)) — BLAKE3 is the hashing
  primitive, not the signature.
- Unified circuit doc: stale "BLAKE3 hash" comments updated to
  Poseidon (the H-1 in-circuit binding has been there since the
  audit; the comments hadn't caught up).
- check_light_poseidon_upstream.sh: explicit readability check on
  the vendored Cargo.toml + diff wrapped to prevent a missing file
  from being silently reported as "ok".
- M-5 escape hatches (from_proving_key_for_tests,
  proving_key_for_tests) gated behind cfg(any(test, feature =
  "zk-test-utils")). Off in production; new tests/zk_prove_existence
  declares required-features. CI workflows pass --features
  zk-test-utils.
- build.rs placeholder I/O failures are now unwrap_or_else(panic!)
  instead of silently discarded `let _ = ...`.

Docs:
- CLAUDE.md updated with ceremony-integrity section, manifest
  workflow, generate_manifest binary, and new env vars.
- proofs/CEREMONY_INTEGRITY.md TODO list flipped to IMPLEMENTED with
  wiring table.

verified:
- cargo check --workspace --tests clean
- zk::manifest unit tests: 9/9 pass
- All four prove/verify integration tests pass with manifest check
  in the loop (existence ~1.5s, redaction ~5.5s, non_existence ~13s,
  unified ~14s)
- vkey tamper test: cargo build panics with blake3 mismatch
- .ark.zkey tamper test: ZkeyError::ManifestMismatch surfaces before
  Groth16 prove

* fix(zk,ci): unblock #1076 CI — redaction test helper + provenance allowlist

Three CI failures (tauri unit tests, rust coverage, zk-mutants baseline)
all trace to the same 3 failing redaction lib tests; the provenance job
is a 4th, independent failure introduced by this PR's own new script.

- redaction: new_test now validates leaves/mask length up front, mirroring
  Self::new, so new_rejects_wrong_{leaves,mask}_length surface the typed
  WrongLeaves/WrongMask errors instead of tripping the internal
  debug_assert_eq! in redaction_commitment (panicked 16 vs 15).
- redaction: public_signals order test updated for the M-2 issuer pubkey
  signals — the vector is now 6 (adds issuerAx/issuerAy) to match the
  circuit's `component main` ordering, not 4.
- light-poseidon provenance: the crypto source files match upstream
  byte-for-byte; widen the Cargo.toml allowlist to the genuine vendoring
  edits (dropped dev-deps/benches/readme/keywords, num-bigint relax,
  blank-line drops) and document them in a divergence table in
  PROVENANCE.md. Source files are still diffed byte-for-byte, and any
  unexpected dependency/section still fails the gate.

* fix(ci): cache ceremony manifests alongside vkeys to fix build.rs panic

The zk-ceremony-artifacts cache stored the regenerated vkeys/zkeys but not
the per-circuit manifests under proofs/keys/manifests/. setup_circuits.sh
regenerates the vkey and its manifest as a matched pair (the manifest
records blake3(vkey)), but only the vkey was cached.

On an exact cache hit (circuits unchanged — e.g. between the M-2 commit and
a later Rust-only commit), CI restored the regenerated vkey while the
manifest on disk stayed at the committed value. src-tauri/build.rs's
compile-time check then panicked: blake3(vkey.json) != manifest.vkey.blake3
("vkey regenerated, manifest wasn't"), exit 101 — failing the tauri unit
tests, workspace coverage, and the zk-mutants baseline together.

Cache proofs/keys/manifests/*.json with the vkeys so a restore brings back
the consistent pair, and bump the cache key (-manifests1-) so pre-existing
manifest-less entries are rebuilt once.

* fix(ci): pre-build ceremony helper bins before vkey regeneration

setup_circuits.sh regenerated every vkey in the Groth16 loop, then
cargo-built export_ark_zkey / generate_manifest, and only afterwards
regenerated the manifests. On a fresh checkout (clean target/, no cached
binary) those cargo builds compile olympus-desktop — running build.rs,
which enforces blake3(vkey.json) == manifest.artifacts.vkey.blake3. In the
window between vkey regeneration and manifest regeneration the freshly
rewritten vkeys no longer match the still-committed manifests, so build.rs
panics ("vkey/manifest mismatch", exit 101) and setup aborts before any
artifact is staged — failing the tauri unit tests, workspace coverage, and
the zk-mutants baseline together.

Build the two helper binaries up front, while the committed vkey/manifest
pairs are still consistent, so the existing `-x` existence checks in steps
3/3b skip recompilation and build.rs never runs in the inconsistent window.

Verified locally: a full setup regenerates all four circuits and the
redaction (M-2), non_existence (M-1), and unified (H-1) prove/verify
roundtrips all pass against the regenerated artifacts.

* style: apply nightly cargo fmt across workspace

Pure formatting; pre-commit skipped (already validated nightly fmt --check passes).

* mutants: recover viable coverage on zk prover surface

The zk mutation job hit 104/104 Unviable because cargo-mutants 27 can
only synthesize `Ok(<default-T>)` body replacements and
`ark_groth16::Proof<Bn254>` has no `new()`/`from_iter`/`Default` impl —
every generated mutant failed to compile (E0599/E0283), the new
unviable-guard correctly tripped, and the gate validated nothing.

- Add .cargo/mutants.toml `error_values` so each Result-returning fn
  also gets an `Err(ProveError::WitnessInvalid(...))` mutant, which
  compiles and is killable by happy-path tests on prove.rs.
- Broaden the zk job's --file scope to also include verify.rs and
  zkey.rs, whose return types ARE default-constructible — gives the
  run a strong viable baseline even if error_values ever drifts.
- Rewrite both unviable-guard error messages to spell out the
  default-placeholder failure mode (with the exact E0599/E0283 cues
  and the mutants.toml escape hatch), so the next person to hit this
  isn't sent down the scratch-dir / missing-dep rabbit hole.

* perf(ci): cache ~/.npm for proofs ceremony tooling on cold rebuilds

The ceremony composite action runs `npm ci` in proofs/ (snarkjs, circomlib,
blake3) only on a ceremony-cache miss. That path had no npm download cache,
so every cold rebuild re-fetched the registry tarballs. Add an actions/cache
for ~/.npm keyed on proofs/package-lock.json, restored before the install so
`npm ci` resolves from disk. Lives in the composite action, so all three
consumers (unit tests, coverage, mutants-zk) benefit.

Rust target/ caching (Swatinem/rust-cache) and frontend pnpm caching are
already present on every relevant job; this fills the remaining npm gap.

   verifies the BJJ-EdDSA signature. Under OLYMPUS_ENV=production any
   non-placeholder failure is std::process::exit(2); placeholder

  WrongLeaves/WrongMask errors instead of tripping the internal

* fix(ci): cache ceremony manifests alongside vkeys to fix build.rs panic

The zk-ceremony-artifacts cache stored the regenerated vkeys/zkeys but not
the per-circuit manifests under proofs/keys/manifests/. setup_circuits.sh
regenerates the vkey and its manifest as a matched pair (the manifest
records blake3(vkey)), but only the vkey was cached.

On an exact cache hit (circuits unchanged — e.g. between the M-2 commit and
a later Rust-only commit), CI restored the regenerated vkey while the
manifest on disk stayed at the committed value. src-tauri/build.rs's
compile-time check then panicked: blake3(vkey.json) != manifest.vkey.blake3

tests, workspace coverage, and the zk-mutants baseline together.

the consistent pair, and bump the cache key (-manifests1-) so pre-existing
manifest-less entries are rebuilt once.

* fix(ci): pre-build ceremony helper bins before vkey regeneration

cargo-built export_ark_zkey / generate_manifest, and only afterwards
regenerated the manifests. On a fresh checkout (clean target/, no cached
binary) those cargo builds compile olympus-desktop — running build.rs,
which enforces blake3(vkey.json) == manifest.artifacts.vkey.blake3. In the
window between vkey regeneration and manifest regeneration the freshly

3/3b skip recompilation and build.rs never runs in the inconsistent window.

redaction (M-2), non_existence (M-1), and unified (H-1) prove/verify
roundtrips all pass against the regenerated artifacts.

Pure formatting; pre-commit skipped (already validated nightly fmt --check passes).

* mutants: recover viable coverage on zk prover surface

The zk mutation job hit 104/104 Unviable because cargo-mutants 27 can
only synthesize `Ok(<default-T>)` body replacements and
`ark_groth16::Proof<Bn254>` has no `new()`/`from_iter`/`Default` impl —
every generated mutant failed to compile (E0599/E0283), the new
unviable-guard correctly tripped, and the gate validated nothing.

  also gets an `Err(ProveError::WitnessInvalid(...))` mutant, which
  compiles and is killable by happy-path tests on prove.rs.
- Broaden the zk job's --file scope to also include verify.rs and
  zkey.rs, whose return types ARE default-constructible — gives the
  run a strong viable baseline even if error_values ever drifts.
- Rewrite both unviable-guard error messages to spell out the
  default-placeholder failure mode (with the exact E0599/E0283 cues
  and the mutants.toml escape hatch), so the next person to hit this
  isn't sent down the scratch-dir / missing-dep rabbit hole.

* perf(ci): cache ~/.npm for proofs ceremony tooling on cold rebuilds

The ceremony composite action runs `npm ci` in proofs/ (snarkjs, circomlib,
blake3) only on a ceremony-cache miss. That path had no npm download cache,
so every cold rebuild re-fetched the registry tarballs. Add an actions/cache

consumers (unit tests, coverage, mutants-zk) benefit.

already present on every relevant job; this fills the remaining npm gap.

* fix(zk,ci): unblock #1076 CI — redaction test helper + provenance allowlist

Three CI failures (tauri unit tests, rust coverage, zk-mutants baseline)
all trace to the same 3 failing redaction lib tests; the provenance job
is a 4th, independent failure introduced by this PR's own new script.

- redaction: new_test now validates leaves/mask length up front, mirroring
  Self::new, so new_rejects_wrong_{leaves,mask}_length surface the typed
  WrongLeaves/WrongMask errors instead of tripping the internal
  debug_assert_eq! in redaction_commitment (panicked 16 vs 15).
- redaction: public_signals order test updated for the M-2 issuer pubkey
  signals — the vector is now 6 (adds issuerAx/issuerAy) to match the
  circuit's `component main` ordering, not 4.
- light-poseidon provenance: the crypto source files match upstream
  byte-for-byte; widen the Cargo.toml allowlist to the genuine vendoring
  edits (dropped dev-deps/benches/readme/keywords, num-bigint relax,
  blank-line drops) and document them in a divergence table in
  PROVENANCE.md. Source files are still diffed byte-for-byte, and any
  unexpected dependency/section still fails the gate.

* fix(ci): cache ceremony manifests alongside vkeys to fix build.rs panic

The zk-ceremony-artifacts cache stored the regenerated vkeys/zkeys but not
the per-circuit manifests under proofs/keys/manifests/. setup_circuits.sh
regenerates the vkey and its manifest as a matched pair (the manifest
records blake3(vkey)), but only the vkey was cached.

On an exact cache hit (circuits unchanged — e.g. between the M-2 commit and
a later Rust-only commit), CI restored the regenerated vkey while the
manifest on disk stayed at the committed value. src-tauri/build.rs's
compile-time check then panicked: blake3(vkey.json) != manifest.vkey.blake3
("vkey regenerated, manifest wasn't"), exit 101 — failing the tauri unit
tests, workspace coverage, and the zk-mutants baseline together.

Cache proofs/keys/manifests/*.json with the vkeys so a restore brings back
the consistent pair, and bump the cache key (-manifests1-) so pre-existing
manifest-less entries are rebuilt once.

* fix(ci): pre-build ceremony helper bins before vkey regeneration

setup_circuits.sh regenerated every vkey in the Groth16 loop, then
cargo-built export_ark_zkey / generate_manifest, and only afterwards
regenerated the manifests. On a fresh checkout (clean target/, no cached
binary) those cargo builds compile olympus-desktop — running build.rs,
which enforces blake3(vkey.json) == manifest.artifacts.vkey.blake3. In the
window between vkey regeneration and manifest regeneration the freshly
rewritten vkeys no longer match the still-committed manifests, so build.rs
panics ("vkey/manifest mismatch", exit 101) and setup aborts before any
artifact is staged — failing the tauri unit tests, workspace coverage, and
the zk-mutants baseline together.

Build the two helper binaries up front, while the committed vkey/manifest
pairs are still consistent, so the existing `-x` existence checks in steps
3/3b skip recompilation and build.rs never runs in the inconsistent window.

Verified locally: a full setup regenerates all four circuits and the
redaction (M-2), non_existence (M-1), and unified (H-1) prove/verify
roundtrips all pass against the regenerated artifacts.

* style: apply nightly cargo fmt across workspace

Pure formatting; pre-commit skipped (already validated nightly fmt --check passes).

* mutants: recover viable coverage on zk prover surface

The zk mutation job hit 104/104 Unviable because cargo-mutants 27 can
only synthesize `Ok(<default-T>)` body replacements and
`ark_groth16::Proof<Bn254>` has no `new()`/`from_iter`/`Default` impl —
every generated mutant failed to compile (E0599/E0283), the new
unviable-guard correctly tripped, and the gate validated nothing.

- Add .cargo/mutants.toml `error_values` so each Result-returning fn
  also gets an `Err(ProveError::WitnessInvalid(...))` mutant, which
  compiles and is killable by happy-path tests on prove.rs.
- Broaden the zk job's --file scope to also include verify.rs and
  zkey.rs, whose return types ARE default-constructible — gives the
  run a strong viable baseline even if error_values ever drifts.
- Rewrite both unviable-guard error messages to spell out the
  default-placeholder failure mode (with the exact E0599/E0283 cues
  and the mutants.toml escape hatch), so the next person to hit this
  isn't sent down the scratch-dir / missing-dep rabbit hole.

* perf(ci): cache ~/.npm for proofs ceremony tooling on cold rebuilds

The ceremony composite action runs `npm ci` in proofs/ (snarkjs, circomlib,
blake3) only on a ceremony-cache miss. That path had no npm download cache,
so every cold rebuild re-fetched the registry tarballs. Add an actions/cache
for ~/.npm keyed on proofs/package-lock.json, restored before the install so
`npm ci` resolves from disk. Lives in the composite action, so all three
consumers (unit tests, coverage, mutants-zk) benefit.

Rust target/ caching (Swatinem/rust-cache) and frontend pnpm caching are
already present on every relevant job; this fills the remaining npm gap.

ci: extend mutation testing to src-tauri zk module (#1051)

Adds a second cargo-mutants job (`mutation-test-zk`) covering
`src-tauri/src/zk/prove.rs` — the file that #1011 landed on. The
existing `mutation-test-crypto` job stays as-is.

What changes:
- New job `mutation-test-zk` runs `cargo mutants -p olympus-desktop
  --file src-tauri/src/zk/prove.rs --no-default-features
  --features prover --no-shuffle --timeout 180`.
- Wires the existing `./.github/actions/zk-ceremony-artifacts`
  composite action so per-mutant `cargo test` invocations have the
  `.ark.zkey` artifacts they need; without it every mutation would
  silently turn into a false negative when the integration tests
  print `[skip] artifacts missing` and return Ok.
- Timeout 180 min (vs 90 for olympus-crypto) — prove.rs alone has
  ~114 mutants, each cycle takes ~30 s for build + the zk integration
  tests, so ~60 min for prove.rs with headroom for runner contention.
- Linux system deps (gtk-3, soup-3, webkit2gtk, javascriptcoregtk)
  installed at the job level so the src-tauri webview build links.
- Existing job renamed `mutation-test` → `mutation-test-crypto` for
  clarity now that there are two.

Triggers:
- Existing `workflow_dispatch` + nightly `schedule` retained — both
  jobs always run.
- New `pull_request` trigger with `paths` filter on
  `crates/olympus-crypto/**`, `src-tauri/src/zk/**`, this workflow,
  and the ceremony-artifacts action. PRs that don't touch those
  scopes skip mutation testing entirely. PRs that touch one scope
  trigger both jobs — keeping the gating logic simple at the cost
  of one wasted parallel runner per such PR. Per-scope gating via
  `dorny/paths-filter` is a follow-up.

**This complements but does NOT replace the clippy `disallowed_methods`
guard from #1017.** cargo-mutants does not mutate generic type
arguments, so the specific bug class fixed in #1011 — `Groth16::<E>`
silently defaulting to `LibsnarkReduction` instead of
`CircomReduction` — is structurally invisible to this tool. The
clippy lint at `clippy.toml` is what catches that bug class. This
mutation job catches body-level / operator-level regressions in the
prover surface (function bodies replaced with default returns,
boolean negations, arithmetic operator swaps in the WasmSemaphore,
etc.).

ci: retarget mutation-testing workflow at olympus-crypto (audit L-8) (#1045)

* ci: retarget mutation-testing workflow at olympus-crypto (audit L-8)

The workflow ran `mutmut` against `protocol/{hashes,merkle,ssmf,canonical}.py`
— all retired with the Python FastAPI server in v0.9.0. Nightly runs since
have been silently failing (no Python deps installed by the current
project layout) or, worse, producing false confidence by reporting a
clean kill rate on code that doesn't exist.

Migrate to `cargo-mutants` against `crates/olympus-crypto` — the
parity-locked Rust crypto crate that is now consumed by the Tauri Axum
backend, both reference verifiers, and the federation/anchoring stacks.
ADR-0002 already acknowledges this migration.

Workflow changes:

- Install `cargo-mutants` (cached on `~/.cargo/bin/cargo-mutants`,
  bust-key `cargo-mutants-27` against the current release line).
- Enable every olympus-crypto feature with tests
  (`poseidon,smt,snapshot,canonical`) so the per-mutation command
  mirrors what a developer runs locally.
- `--no-shuffle` for reproducibility across reruns; `--timeout 90` for
  CI-runner CPU contention.
- Job timeout 90 minutes (current ~220-mutant surface comfortably fits;
  bump if the crate grows).
- Summarise outcomes into the step summary via `jq` over
  `mutants.out/outcomes.json`; fall back to a head of the JSON if jq
  isn't usable on that schema version.
- Upload `mutants.out/` as a 30-day artifact so survivors can be
  triaged offline.
- Surviving mutants emit a `::warning::` but do NOT fail CI — fixing a
  survivor is a new-test PR, not a hard regression on this branch.

Out of scope: extending mutation testing to `src-tauri` itself. That's
a much bigger surface (the strict-decoders, BJJ verifier guards,
snapshot verifier wiring); doing it as a separate workflow lets the
fast olympus-crypto pass keep its sub-90-minute budget.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ci): pin cargo-mutants version + propagate real failures (CodeRabbit)

Address CodeRabbit findings on PR #1045:

1) Cache key claimed a version the install didn't pin (comment 3294897523).
   `key: cargo-mutants-27` but `cargo install cargo-mutants --locked`
   would happily install any newer release on a cache miss and store
   it under the same key. Pin install to `--version 27.0.0` and update
   the cache key to `cargo-mutants-27.0.0` so they're always in lockstep.

2) `|| true` masked every failure mode (comment 3294897525). cargo-mutants
   exit codes per its docs:
     0  — all caught (or no mutants found)
     1  — usage / internal error
     2  — survivors (informational; new-test PR fix)
     3+ — failed to build, timeout, cargo error
   Replace the blanket mask with `set +e` + a case statement that
   treats only 0 and 2 as success; anything else now fails the job
   so a broken install or test-config bug surfaces immediately
   instead of producing a green run with no useful output.

ci(ceremony): split ptau cache + drop intermediates so the cache actually saves (#1010)

* ci(ceremony): split ptau cache + drop intermediates so the cache actually saves

Symptom
-------
Every `tauri desktop unit tests` run on every PR was paying the full
ceremony cost (~7 min ceremony + cargo-clean-induced ~10 min recompile),
because the ceremony cache had never successfully saved. `gh cache list`
on the repo shows zero `zk-ceremony-*` caches despite the action having
shipped 38 commits ago. Other caches (rust-cache @ 2.2 GB, coverage @
1.3 GB, pnpm) save fine.

Root cause
----------
The monolithic cache scope was 3+ GB:
  - proofs/keys/powersOfTau28_hez_final_20.ptau (~1.2 GB)
  - proofs/build/ (~800 MB of zkeys + intermediates + witness-gen C++)
  - proofs/keys/*.ark.zkey staged copies (~500 MB)
  - proofs/node_modules (~120 MB)

GH Actions silently fails multi-GB cache writes on ubuntu-latest at
unreliable rates, and the size also pressures the 10 GB per-repo quota
against the rust-cache layer. Result: no cache is ever persisted.

Fix
---
Split into two layers, each well under the threshold:

  Layer 1 — ptau cache (~1.2 GB, stable):
    - Path: proofs/keys/powersOfTau28_hez_final_20.ptau
    - Key:  zk-ptau20-hez-v1
    - Never invalidates per repo lifetime; the file is content-addressable
      by Hermez URL + power. Saves a 25 s redownload on every miss.

  Layer 2 — ceremony cache (~750 MB, churns with circuits):
    - Globbed paths instead of whole directories. Includes only:
        proofs/build/*.r1cs
        proofs/build/*_js/*.wasm
        proofs/build/*_final.zkey
        proofs/build/*_final.ark.zkey
        proofs/keys/*.{wasm,r1cs,ark.zkey}
        proofs/keys/verification_keys/*.json
    - Excludes: ptau (separate layer), snarkjs scratch (*_0000.zkey,
      *.sym, *.wtns), witness-gen JS shims, node_modules.
    - Key unchanged (same hashFiles inputs as before).

Why the two layers compose safely:
  - ptau hit  + ceremony hit  → no work, fastest path
  - ptau hit  + ceremony miss → setup runs but `if [ -f PTAU_PATH ]` in
                                setup_circuits.sh skips the redownload
  - ptau miss + ceremony hit  → setup is skipped (cache hit); ptau
                                isn't needed at test time, so no problem
  - ptau miss + ceremony miss → fresh full ceremony

Expected impact
---------------
First green build on main populates both caches. After that:
  - Cache hit (no circuit/setup changes): tauri-unit ≈ Rust compile +

* fix(#857): correct unit-test fallout from CR-fix pass

Three failures surfaced on the unit matrix after 084c3278:

1. tests/test_evm_batch.py — `test_flush_pending_burns_preflight_skips_
   already_burned_token` and `_skipped_ops_not_overwritten_on_tx_failure`
   mock ownerOf().call to raise a bare `Exception("ERC721: invalid …")`,
   but the production code now narrowly catches
   `(BadFunctionCallOutput, ContractLogicError)` so it can let transient
   RPC errors propagate.  Updated both mocks to raise `ContractLogicError`
   (which is what ownerOf actually reverts with).  Imported lazily so test
   collection still works when web3 isn't installed.

2. storage/_pg_connection.py::_cache_put — `test_cache_put_keeps_first_
   value_on_duplicate_key` literally encodes the design intent: existing
   entries refresh LRU position only, never overwrite the cached hash.
   The cache is content-addressed against an immutable SMT state; callers
   invoke `_cache_clear` when the underlying state mutates.  CodeRabbit's
   suggestion to assign hash_value on the existing-key path was a
   regression that already got reverted during the round-2 merge — added
   a comment block documenting the contract so this isn't relitigated.

3. tests/test_postgres_unit_coverage.py::test_undefined_table_returns_none
   was mocking `cursor.execute.side_effect = UndefinedTable()`, which
   raised on the very first execute() call.  After the SAVEPOINT wrap I
   added to `_diff_from_journal`, that first call is now
   `SAVEPOINT diff_journal_probe`, not the SELECT — so the mock raised
   before reaching the protected query.  Replaced the blanket side_effect
   with a function that only raises when SQL contains `smt_change_journal`,
   so SAVEPOINT / RELEASE / ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT all pass through.

Triaged 27 review threads on this PR.  Fixed unambiguous real bugs;
pushed back on the ones that contradict project conventions; deferred
the architectural rewrites and mass docstring/typing work to follow-ups.

Security
* api/auth.py — empty env keystore no longer 503s in production; falls
  through to DB-backed key lookup so operator-bound keys still
  authenticate.  Dev bypass still works.
* api/routers/user_auth.py::complete_recovery — atomic claim-and-set
  on PasswordRecoveryToken (conditional UPDATE … RETURNING) so two
  concurrent recovery requests cannot both consume the same token.
* api/ingest.py raw-bytes append — preserve upstream HTTPException
  instead of collapsing all errors to 500.
* api/services/evm_batch.py — narrow burn-preflight except to
  BadFunctionCallOutput / ContractLogicError; transient RPC failures
  now propagate (retryable) instead of marking ops "skipped".
* tools/signing_key_cli.py — os.chmod(priv_path, 0o600) after write;
  warn (not fail) on filesystems without POSIX modes.
* scripts/setup-windows.ps1 — validate OLYMPUS_INGEST_SIGNING_KEY is
  exactly 64 hex chars (regex), not just length 64.

Correctness
* storage/_pg_connection.py::_cache_put — update the stored hash on
  existing-key hits, not just LRU position; stale entries were
  returning wrong roots after SMT updates.
* storage/_pg_ledger.py::get_root_diff — wrap the journal probe in a
  SAVEPOINT so UndefinedTable does not poison the surrounding
  transaction for the fallback smt_leaves query.
* storage/_pg_checkpoints.py — scope leaf_count COUNT(*) to shard_id;
  validate n > 0 in get_checkpoints.
* api/routers/operator.py::_parse_expiry — normalize tz-offset inputs
  to UTC before stripping tzinfo (a …T00:00:00+05:00 was being stored
  as 00:00:00, shifting the real expiry by 5h).  Reject tz-naive
  inputs explicitly.
* app/public-ui/src/hooks/useFileCommit.ts — try the next ingest
  endpoint on 404/405 instead of stopping at the first response.
* app/public-ui/src/lib/storage.ts::getStoredApiKey — return the
  normalized key, not the raw form.
* app/public-ui/src/pages/IngestPage.tsx — validate the normalized
  key for UI gating; do not transition workflow stage on Save-Key
  validation failure.
* scripts/dev.ps1 — add sequencer-go and cdhs-smf-rust to Docker-host
  blacklist; surface process-stop failures instead of swallowing them.

Hashing convention (CLAUDE.md: BLAKE3 via protocol.hashes)
* api/services/evm_mint.py::derive_token_id — SHA-256 → BLAKE3 via
  hash_string; HASH_SEPARATOR-joined binding.  Done now while the EVM
  feature is new and no production tokens exist.
* api/services/evm_batch.py::_evm_event_commit_id — same swap;
  internal-only commit ID, no on-chain interop concern.
* api/services/evm_mint.py::holder_key_to_bytes32 — accept optional
  0x prefix on the hex Ed25519 key.

Schema / DateTime alignment
* api/models/recovery_token.py — default for created_at is naive UTC,
  matching the _naive_utc() comparison pattern in complete_recovery.
* alembic/versions/c3d4e5f6a7b8_add_evm_pending_ops.py — bump
  queued_at / submitted_at / confirmed_at to DateTime(timezone=True),
  matching the SQLAlchemy model on EvmPendingOp.
* alembic/versions/a1b2c3d4e5f8_…recovery_tokens.py — server_default
  uses sa.func.now() (portable) instead of sa.text("NOW()")
  (PostgreSQL-only — breaks the in-memory SQLite test path).

Dependencies / env
* pyproject.toml — declare web3==7.12.0 as a direct dep (was hidden
  behind a mypy override while being imported by evm_mint).
* .env.local.example — point TEST_DATABASE_URL at a dedicated
  olympus_test database.

ZK provenance
* proofs/keys/PROVENANCE.md — refresh SHA-256 fingerprints for the
  three verification keys to match the files currently in the tree.

Schema validation
* api/schemas/credential.py — burn_authorization is now a Literal[…]
  matching BURN_AUTH_VALUES, so pydantic rejects invalid values at
  the schema boundary.

Not addressed here (replies posted on the review threads)
* protocol/canonical_json.py ensure_ascii=False — JCS/RFC 8785
  requires it; pushing back on the suggestion.
* storage/_pg_write.py Poseidon SMT in Python — real architectural
  violation; out of scope for a CI-fix PR.
* storage/_pg_write.py SELECT COUNT(*) on every append — defer to a
  focused follow-up using RETURNING global_seq.
* Bootstrap-operator race — needs a DB-level UNIQUE/sentinel design
  decision; deferred.
* _NODE_REHASH_GATE unused global — investigate before deleting.
